A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same two-stage black-box prompt-poisoning work, renamed from CAIN to SPECTRE. All pages, equations, tables, figures and appendices were readable and supported comparison across the substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original TriviaQA and TruthfulQA experiments, commercial-model evaluations, ablations and a scientific peer-review case study.

after.justification: v3 retains original QA experiments and adds ECLIPSE comparisons, targeted commercial-model results, defense evaluations and supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: The AAP initialization and greedy word-perturbation pipeline remain. However, Sections 3–4 revise the documented optimization objective and replace the earlier F1-difference initialization score with an indicator-based success score. These are changes to the specified scoring procedure; the PDFs do not establish a new implemented pipeline or reruns of retained experiments.

E1.justification: TriviaQA, the six TruthfulQA categories and the two-option/four-option/free-form scenarios are retained; the renamed Concept Corruption Test already existed. Auxiliary coverage changes: v2's ICLR 2025 peer-review case study disappears, while v3 adds real-world tool-prompt examples and evaluation under prompt filtering and sanitization.

E2.justification: ECLIPSE, previously discussed but not evaluated, becomes an external attack comparator in the untargeted and targeted comparisons, including Tables 2–3 and A6. It also participates in the new detection comparison. The existing NSP, Manual, AAP and initialization comparators remain.

E3.justification: New protocols include ECLIPSE with population 20 and 50 iterations, optimization without typo perturbations, detector evaluations, GPT-4o-mini prompt sanitization and targeted testing on commercial APIs. Existing QA metrics and principal splits remain documented. However, v3 Appendix B.1 inconsistently specifies 100 versus 10 held-out target paraphrases, preventing a reliable claim that this existing split changed.

E4.justification: v3 adds a typo-removal ablation, detector and sanitization tests, train/evaluation semantic-overlap analysis, natural-typo examples and additional attack cases. It removes v2's perplexity-distribution analysis and peer-review case study. Threshold, benign-set-size, model-size and initialization analyses are largely retained or relocated.

E5.justification: v2 Appendix A.2 specifies sampling seed 42; v3 omits this information. Neither version supplies a clear repeated-run count or introduces confidence intervals or significance testing. Shaded bands in retained sensitivity plots do not constitute a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Retained rows in Tables 2–4 and the additional untargeted table are numerically unchanged after matching method names. Substantial new results include ECLIPSE scores, targeted API outcomes such as 84.00 malicious F1 for GPT-3.5-Turbo in free-form evaluation, and defense results. Some new entries are inconsistent: Table A6 reports ECLIPSE's gap as -30.02 despite benign/malicious F1 values of 12.52/9.46. Peer-review and perplexity results are removed.

T1.justification: Section 3 substantially revises the formal problem. v2 separately defines untargeted and targeted losses, with the targeted loss explicitly penalizing the correct target answer. v3 replaces these with a joint malicious-output and benign-output objective and adds a perplexity upper bound alongside semantic similarity in a finite-length token space. These formulations are not mathematically equivalent; neither version supplies theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: Selective black-box corruption with benign preservation remains the central contribution. v3 adds an approximately $2-per-target efficiency claim and explicitly extends defense-evasion claims to typo correction. Its abstract changes the headline F1 reduction from 40% to 70%, although the principal retained performance tables are unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 interprets format transfer as altered internal reasoning, attributes optimization success to permissible typo noise, and explains sanitization resistance through semantic steering. These go beyond v2's transferability discussion. It also adds substantive single-turn, benchmark-coverage and absent-human-study limitations, while removing the peer-review failure interpretation and the explicit limitation concerning models larger than 32B.

D1.justification: v3 adds stage-specific cost estimates, ECLIPSE configuration, the sanitization prompt and a source for real-world prompt examples. Hardware, quantization and free-form answer mapping remain. Conversely, it omits v2's m=7 benign-success requirement, F1 stopping cutoffs and 150-word maximum prompt length. These are documentation changes, not evidence that the corresponding settings were changed.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially repositioned around persistent system-prompt poisoning versus jailbreaking, training-time backdoors and indirect prompt injection. New discussion and citations include sleeper agents, instruction-tuning poisoning, many-shot and multi-turn attacks, OPRO and INSEC, supported by a new taxonomy table. Earlier psychological and prompt-trigger positioning is reduced or removed.

P1.justification: The title and method are renamed, and the abstract, introduction, related work, formulation, method explanations and results narrative are extensively rewritten. v3 introduces a supply-chain and permissible-noise narrative, reorganizes the appendix into methodological, experimental, quantitative and qualitative sections, and separates limitations and ethical considerations.

P2.justification: v3 redraws the opening threat illustration, adds typo-ablation, detection and sanitization plots, expands comparison tables and adds qualitative displays. Existing threshold and benign-size plots move between the main text and appendix, and targeted initialization tables are merged. The perplexity plot disappears. Typography, captions, prompt boxes and page layout also change extensively.

improvement.justification: The external baseline, direct defense tests and explicit single-turn and human-study limitations strengthen v3's empirical scrutiny. However, it introduces contradictory paraphrase counts and incorrect ECLIPSE gap calculations, removes reproducibility-critical stopping details, and draws stronger internal-reasoning conclusions from retained format-transfer evidence. These substantive gains and new reliability problems leave the net direction of overall quality uncertain.
